title: Choose checked for the recoverable failure and unchecked for the bug

blocks.text: Whether an exception is checked should follow from whether the client can reasonably be expected to recover from it. `Gateway` has two failures; give each exception the right superclass (`Exception` or `RuntimeException`) and write the method.

items: `RateLimitedException(String message, int retryAfterSeconds)` with `getRetryAfterSeconds()`: the caller sent too much and may simply try again later.
`BadRequestIdException(String message)`: the caller passed no request id, which is a programming error.
a `null` or blank id throws `BadRequestIdException("Request id is required")`;
more than `10` calls this minute throws `RateLimitedException("Rate limit exceeded", 60)`;

cases.says: A good request is sent; too many calls throw RateLimitedException and an empty id throws BadRequestIdException.
RateLimitedException is checked, because a caller can recover by retrying, and it carries how long to wait.
BadRequestIdException is unchecked, because a missing id is a bug in the caller that no retry fixes.
A blank or null id is as bad as an empty one.

concepts: Whether a caller can reasonably recover decides between a checked and an unchecked exception.
